clue.text: Spectacular sort of rise crack CEO merits (almost)

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: taken as written before its trim

explanation.surface: A brilliant chief executive's merits supposedly earned a dazzling promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MERITS to MERIT; 'crack' shuffles CEO plus MERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteoric rise is one as sudden and brilliant as a shooting star across the sky.

clue.text: Secret agents furious, having nothing on arch-enemy?

indicators.note: having means the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: furious means mad, very angry

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
the Nazi SS, the arch-enemy of the Jewish people

explanation.surface: Spies in a rage with nothing on their greatest foe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mossad is Israel's national intelligence service, so its people are secret agents.

clue.text: America's part in the Fourth Estate, say

indicators.note: part in the means the letters sit within the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A remark about the role the United States plays in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fourTH ESTATE Say; the Fourth Estate is the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans and others commonly call the United States of America simply by this short name.

clue.text: Grandad's brief role in Othello, apparently

definitions.text: Grandad's brief role in Othello, apparently

parts.words: Grandad's brief role in Othello, apparently
parts.note: OAP, the brief form of the answer, is tucked inside othellO APparently, so a grandad's abbreviation has a part in the play

explanation.walkthrough: The letters O, A, P straddle 'Othello apparently'; 'brief' says those letters are an abbreviation, which a retired grandad would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical grandad, retired and drawing a state pension, is what Britons call an OAP.

clue.text: Native American once, a member of 2

parts.note: Indian is the older, now dated name for a Native American

explanation.surface: An indigenous American of old, one of the nation's peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is the answer to 2 down, the American states, of which this is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it belongs to that union.

clue.text: Course not taken in mixed-ability group

definitions.meaning: in British schools pupils are grouped by ability into ...; a mixed-ability class does without that

explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a course of water, and a school set of pupils of similar ability is the other sense.

clue.text: Lapidarian superinjunctions from on high

parts.note: God's laws were carved in stone tablets (lapidarian) and were sweeping orders handed down from heaven

explanation.walkthrough: A superinjunction is a British court order so strict that even its existence cannot be reported.

clue.text: English soak up what can be seen on the piste

definitions.text: what can be seen on the piste

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to soak is to seep through

explanation.surface: An Englishman absorbs what he sees on the ski slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEEP into PEES. The piste here is a fencing strip, not a ski run.
explanation.definitionFit: The piste is the strip on which fencers compete with these swords.

clue.text: Omit part of text, reportedly, being set out wrongly

indicators.note: reportedly means what is said aloud gives the letters

parts.note: to skip a row of writing is to miss a line

explanation.surface: Leaving out some text through badly laid-out typesetting.
explanation.definitionFit: To misalign something is to set it out in the wrong position or out of true.

clue.text: Anglo-French country without a language

parts.note: AF is the abbreviation for Anglo-French

indicators.note: without means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: Ghana is a West African country

explanation.surface: A hybrid Anglo-French nation that has no tongue of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghan is another name for Pashto, a tongue spoken in Afghanistan.

clue.text: Race in which horse loses time but gains power

indicators.note: loses means one letter goes from the word
but gains means another letter comes in its place

parts.note: a steed is a horse
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A racehorse that slows down yet builds up strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to go at great speed, to hurry along fast.

clue.text: They support shelves around a central point

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps round the second

an end is a point, here sitting at the centre of the word

explanation.surface: Brackets holding up shelving set round a middle spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelves' is a verb, not plural furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenders stand up for a cause or person, so they back it.

clue.text: Sign TA group has mostly reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims HAS to HA; 'reformed' shuffles TA, GROUP and HA. The TA is Britain's Territorial Army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To autograph something is to put your signature on it.

clue.text: Parasite's head attaches to tail of bird

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.walkthrough: Moving the L of LOUSE to the end gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird and related thrushes.

clue.text: More work actually impossible to find

definitions.meaning: a book by Sir Thomas More
the name means no place in Greek, so it cannot really be found

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's book imagines an ideal island state, whose Greek name means nowhere.

clue.text: One helps identify suspect meat in a horse!

clue.text: Seek out a path from the trig point?

definitions.text: a path from the trig point?

clue.text: Pub rules? A few lines in black and white

definitions.text: A few lines in black and white

parts.note: a bar is a pub
codes are sets of rules

clue.text: Side weapons are kept here

clue.text: What's clearly required for swimming class

definitions.meaning: read as two words: fewer clothes on

clue.text: A hunt's lost in protective cover

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, with its S

clue.text: Poles stuck in trail for support

parts.note: a spoor is an animal's track or trail

explanation.surface: Polish people stuck on a path, asking for backing.

clue.text: You may be putting on these for a party

definitions.meaning: golfers putt on the smooth grass around each hole
the Green Party, an environmentalist political group

I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A raccoon-skin jacket comes with one.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted mammal of the raccoon family from the Americas.

clue.text: A kind of mind necessary for management

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: kind of means a version of the word, its letters rearranged

minions are underlings

explanation.definitionFit: Dominions are powers of rule, or the territories over which a sovereign rules.

clue.text: Presently rejected eastern method of execution

parts.note: presently means soon

clue.text: Various fruit growers do it with tomatoes

definitions.text: fruit growers do it with tomatoes
definitions.meaning: tomatoes are often dried in the sun
